projects.title: Guesscasso
projects.description: Built an innovative multiplayer guessing game that flips the traditional Pictionary concept on its head using diffusion models and LLMs that won 1st place at the 2025 Machine Learning at Berkeley Hackathon! Instead of humans drawing, players race to guess what AI diffusion models are creating in real-time. Guesscasso combines two random words (think "dinosaur-cowboy") and challenges players to decipher the AI's artistic interpretation as the image gradually denoises. Engineered a full-stack solution with Flux.1 for image generation, Llama 3.3 for guess evaluation and feedback, Python/Flask backend leveraging Groq for rapid inference, React/Next.js frontend for seamless multiplayer experience, and integrated Gradio for smooth AI model deployment.

My summer at Uber was out of this world! I interned with the Uber AI Solutions team, AKA Project Moonshot, to: • build out a robust backend service for a feature management tool • architect SQL databases for complex feature and account hierarchies • develop multi-modal CLIP models to generate image embeddings and ingest them into an OpenSearch cluster • deploy an experimental contextual search engine with agent workflows for embedding natural language text queries and performing KNN vector searches over relevant images Being a part of mission control as we launched Uber AI Solutions in July was an exhilarating experience—I’m forever grateful I got the chance to contribute to Uber’s initiative to power the foundations of the AI revolution: data labeling, generation, and collection. And that’s only scratching the surface of what Uber AI Solutions is doing 🚀 My Uber internship really helped me widen my orbit. Whether it was seeing the forest and the trees 🌲 while engineering scalable databases from the ground up, leveraging a go-get-it 🏎️ mindset to turn research on multi-modal deep-learning models into a deployed proof of concept, staying curious and communicative with my team because great minds don’t think alike 🧠, or building with heart ❤️ as I navigated technical challenges to make the biggest impact I could on my team, our users, and the world, I’ve felt my horizons expand faster than the speed of light! A sincere thank you to my galactic team, and my manager Abhishek Shiroor , mentor Talon Jin , and recruiter Vicki C. for helping my passions take-off this summer 🪐 ...more

Launching the UC Berkeley M.E.T. (Management, Entrepreneurship, and Technology) Program in New York City was exhilarating, insightful, and beyond anything I could have imagined! I spent a week (about the same amount of time a round-trip journey to the moon takes!) exploring just a few of the countless diverse and innovative industries thriving in New York City: Blackstone , Sony Music Entertainment , NBCUniversal , NYSE , Warby Parker , Whop , Brooklyn Nets , Cockroach Labs , and Veronica Beard. Along the way, I learned a couple of things to help my own moonshot ideas take off: 🌟 Lean into disruption Whether you are experiencing disruption or acting as a catalyst for it, embrace change as an opportunity to meaningfully impact our world. Growth happens when we dare to step outside of our comfort zones and initiate bold revolutions. The most revolutionary ideas often come from challenging the status quo and rethinking what’s possible—it’s hard to look past the limits of our known universe in search of disruption, but also incredibly transformative when we do! 🌟 Surround yourself with incredible people Surrounding yourself with brilliant minds, diverse perspectives, and passionate peers creates an environment where you can continually learn and be inspired. Seek out communities where you are challenged and empowered. Together, you can ignite each other’s fires and become trailblazers! 🌟 Always stay curious Curiosity is the fuel for moonshot thinking. The world is vast and curiosity is a spark that lights our way as we explore it. Exploration leads to discovery, even if the path isn’t linear or predictable. Whether it’s diving into a new field, experimenting with unconventional ideas, or simply asking “what if?”, curiosity keeps innovation alive. A cosmic thank you to everyone who helped me shoot for the stars! Saikat Chaudhuri , Chris Dito , Dawn Kramer, Aileen Ghosh , Katie DuPlessis , Jagreet Sekhon , and everyone on-site and behind the scenes who made this experience possible, you are all superstars. Thank you for helping my dreams and this trip take off! To everyone who welcomed us into their companies, thank you for inspiring us with your stories of the infinite ways innovation can take place! And to my best friends who took this adventure with me, thank you for the lifelong memories I will always cherish—from challenging each other to think even more creatively while strategizing disruptors to help Cockroach Labs position themselves for the future of database innovation, to side-questing with me at jazz clubs and comedy shows, to accompanying me on our Apollo Bagels excursions, to dancing our hearts out with Professor Saikat at the Brooklyn Nets game! Looking forward to blasting off with this unforgettable experience! 🚀 ...more

Prompt is Hex's first-ever customer conference. One day in San Francisco, entirely about data in the age of AI. Big talks, real conversations, and hands-on workshops with the people actually building and thinking about this stuff. You'll leave with things that hold up on Monday, not just a tote bag. Come find out what a data conference feels like when it's actually good. Reach out to prompt@hex.tech to book your spot!

We just released Evals in the Hex platform, based on everything we've learned from the last 2 years building out our own internal eval tools. Some highlights: - LLM-as-a-judge rubrics that allow for actually nuanced grading - model sweeps, so you can test new models as they come out - everything is code defined so using an agent for setup is a breeze, and every change is tracked in git Let us know what you think!

The latest shift in the role of data teams: maintaining and managing analytics agents. The Chime ® data team built their own eval harness to do this. They ran questions one-by-one against the agent and graded each with an LLM-as-judge they had to tune and maintain by hand to keep up with 50+ domains. To make this easier for teams like Chime, we're introducing Evals in Hex. Measure how the Hex Agent performs and test context changes safely before they ship, all from the CLI.

I had the pleasure of presenting Hex 's approach to data analytics benchmarking at this year's Agentic AI Summit! You can watch me speak here: https://lnkd.in/eR2BbqFn TL;DR: Existing data benchmarks are unrealistic and incomplete, so we built our own: with a realistic synthetic environment to match! At Hex, we spend a ton of time thinking about how to best evaluate models on their ability to do complex analytical tasks. It's a super nontrivial problem, and we're looking forward to sharing more on this, so keep your eyes peeled for incoming blog posts 👀 Massive massive thank you to Izzy Miller for graciously allowing me to co-opt his slides, and for taking time after his workday to help me workshop this talk. I *highly* recommend watching his original talk— the version I gave was cut down to a speedy 5 minutes, but Izzy goes into many of the juicy details here: https://lnkd.in/ehgp3pED If you're interested in thinking about these problems, Hex might be the place for you! Don't hesitate to reach out :)

Today marks a week since I joined Hex in New York City, and it has been an incredible start to learning about this amazingly complex yet intuitive product, meeting some of the most talented people in the startup space, and embracing the experience of becoming a "data person" by dogfooding the best AI analytics platform. I can't wait to start helping customers unlock the value of Hex as part of the Sales team. 🧙‍♀️🔮 Ever since I started college at the University of Southern California , I was on a mission to figure out what I wanted to do after graduation (also, I'm thrilled to share that I graduated on the Dean's List after the best four years of my life 💛❤️). Throughout that journey, one thing became clear: I wanted to work for a company creating real impact by solving a real problem that I'd experienced firsthand. That's exactly what Hex does. It empowers teams that love working with data and those who are just getting started to explore, analyze, and collaborate in a way that feels conversational. It enables every member on every team to get trusted answers grounded in the organization's data, and share insights with others seamlessly (and so much more). A special thank you to Greg Reardon and Emily (Turner) Sutley for guiding me through the recruiting process and helping me get here, and to Ali Chinetti for the warmest welcome on her team. I'm grateful to be joining Hex at such an exciting time as the product continues to get better every day. Here's to what's next!🌟

All gas no brakes this July 🏎️ 💨 Here’s what our team shipped this month: - Brand your generative apps with a design.md file - Directly edit generative app code - Download any chart or table as a CSV - Improved screenshot tooling for generative apps - Get notified when the agent needs you or is finished - Set a default model for the agent - Switch between Kimi K2.7, Fable 5, and Opus 5 at your hearts desire - Access Context Studio data and the agent via CLI - See what resources the agent uses most - See your cell outputs via CLI - Faster schema refreshes for Snowflake - Set workspace spend limits for auto top-ups - Set custom add-on allocations for specific users or groups Get the full rundown at the link in the comments ⬇️

Here are some recent quotes I have heard from actual Hex customers: “We’re HUGE fans of the platform” “Honestly, I am in awe” "I think this might be the first BI tool I've used that's good.” “I’m so f**king fired up about this agentic analytics stuff…I can’t sleep” “This has changed the way I evaluate data tooling” It’s been a while since I’ve heard this type of enthusiasm about a data product. So, we decided to host an event bringing all these crazy, excited people together. It’s called Prompt. We’ll have some leading thinkers talking about where this is all going, some hands-on sessions where you can put it all into practice, and some other fun ways for you to connect and nerd out. It’s also super duper exclusive (not really that exclusive, but we’re not opening it up to just anybody). If you want to join, hit me up.
